title: Whole psalter allocation with inherited references, split units and weekly coverage
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED. Complete Regula Benedicti18 binds repeated references to the same psalm parts and hours, while splitting/merging units and preserving full weekly coverage under an expressly permitted alternative arrangement. Coverage is not150utterances.

design.structural_baseline: Directed word composition, hierarchy at spaces, whole-form residuals and entry effects are known structural constraints, not identified phonemes, morphemes or meanings. A hypothetical whole reading is allowed without confirmed seedwords; none is asserted here.
design.writer_limit: No finite Voynich writer is selected. No EVA=Latin alphabet, one-source-clause=one-word, fixed paragraph heading/count, per-occurrence key or unexplained filler is licensed. This is raw source-content supply.
design.access: No raw target packet/image/reserve/new manuscript admission; no GDT990 model or results. A historical proposal source_evidence quote unexpectedly exposed four old target groups during duplicate navigation; no use was made of them.
selection_debts: Nominate a complete already admitted target unit before any fitting; retain all groups and boundary alternatives.
Specify a finite globally shared realization and reference policy; test a full competing interpretation rather than a few short fragments.
Keep source interpretation, modern content representation and target realization distinct.
design.review_limit: Bounded route/topic/registry screens, not exhaustive primary review; RAW status is intentional.

source_evidence.quote: ## A. Benedict18: Wiederaufnahme, Teilung und Wochenabschluss

source.historical_date: Sixth-century work; BKV names Benedict of Nursia480–547. This is a digital Latin edition, not a newly collated medieval manuscript.
source.boundary: [1] In primis through [25] ...septimana integra persolvamus; all25verses.
source.edition_limit: The accompanying German translation says first/third/sixth at Monday Prime, while the displayed Latin says primus/secundus/sextus. This card owns the Latin branch and does not silently harmonize the conflict. Earlier office instructions are external prerequisite calls, not re-created here.

design.historical_writing_mechanism: The written expressions suprascripti, residua, idem, per easdem horas and sicut supra refer to previously delimited texts/slots; incipit and gloria summon known longer utterances. These are actual prose reference conventions, not an invented cipher.
whole_content_model: Invocation/Gloria and hour hymn precede assigned psalms.
Sunday Prime uses four sections of118; Sunday lesser hours use three sections each. Monday lesser hours consume the nine residual sections.
Monday Prime starts1,2,6; following Prime sequences advance through19, splitting9and17. Sunday vigils begin20.
Tuesday lesser hours assign119–127 in three groups and repeat those groups at the same hours through the week.
Vespers use109–147 with the source exclusions;138/143/144split,116joins115; its remaining service elements invoke earlier instructions.
Compline repeats4,90,133. Remaining psalms go to seven vigils, dividing longer ones and setting twelve for each night.

An alternative distribution is explicitly permitted only with the entire150-psalm corpus covered each week and Sunday restart. The exhortation contrasts ancient daily completion with present weekly duty.
design.coupled_consequence: References to the remaining sections inherit a cursor into the same118, while daily repeated groups inherit the same hour allocation. Splitting and joining change performance slots without creating/deleting psalm identity. The whole-week invariant covers150distinct canonical psalms while allowing required repetitions; an exact150-event invariant is false.

precise_rivals.rule: Reset the118part reference at every new day.
precise_rivals.different_consequence: Reuses Sunday sections instead of Monday residual sections; the complete118is not consumed as stated.

precise_rivals.rule: Every canonical psalm is one indivisible hour unit.
precise_rivals.different_consequence: Cannot preserve both the expressly split long psalms and joined115/116.

precise_rivals.rule: Any valid weekly allocation has exactly150performed items.
precise_rivals.different_consequence: Contradicts explicit daily repeated psalms and the distinction between coverage and utterance count.

finite_semantic_restrictions: Day and hour roles are shared across the whole section; no per-occurrence calendar interpretation.
Whole-psalm identity and section identity are distinct. A join preserves two psalm identities, a split preserves one.
The optional alternative schedule is source-licensed, but full coverage and restart are nonoptional.
unknowns_and_likely_failure: The full text of each referenced psalm and prior office templates are external calls; this packet owns the entire chapter18instruction, not a complete performance of all150psalms.
No manuscript target owns a canonical text corpus, weekday or hour here. Without a finite realization the structure could merely relabel a general allocation program.
The Latin primus/secundus/sextus conflicts with the accompanying German first/third/sixth; only the Latin branch is proposed.

design.smallest_future_decision: Only consider a target experiment once a full paragraph hypothesis has recurrent references with an independently fixed whole/part distinction. A mere list of day names or matched total cannot select this meaning.
